contract_plain_english: For a fixed probability space and a strictly positive exponent below one, define the finite L^p quantity of a real random variable by ∥X∥_{L^p} = (E|X|^p)^{1/p}. The source says that the usual triangle inequality on the resulting L^p space fails, so this quantity is not a norm. It does not provide a counterexample, quantify the ambient probability spaces precisely, or assert any quasi-norm inequality. [E1, E2, E3, E4, E5]
